subject: Archaeology
title: The Sunken Pharos of Alexandria
description: One-minute skill: The Sunken Pharos of Alexandria.

hook.text: The Lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

buildup.text: Built around 280 BCE, the Pharos stood over 300 feet tall and guided ships into Alexandria for over 1,000 years.

discovery.text: Earthquakes between 956 and 1323 CE gradually toppled it. Divers found massive stone blocks on the harbor floor in 1994.

twist.text: Qaitbay Fortress, built on the lighthouse site in 1480, used some of the fallen lighthouse stones in its own walls.

climax.text: Underwater surveys mapped over 2,500 blocks from the lighthouse.

punchline.text: A Wonder of the World fell into the sea. Its stones built a medieval fort.

quiz.question: What happened to the Pharos Lighthouse of Alexandria?
options: It was deliberately demolished by conquering armies
Earthquakes gradually toppled it into the harbor between 956 and 1323 CE
It was dismantled and shipped to Rome by Emperor Augustus

details.summary: The Pharos of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, collapsed into the sea after earthquakes in the 14th century. Underwater surveys have located massive stone blocks, sphinxes, and column fragments from the lighthouse scattered across the seafloor near Qaitbay Fort.
details.whyItMatters: The Pharos was the world's first lighthouse and the tallest non-pyramid structure of the ancient world. Finding its remains underwrites confirms ancient descriptions and provides physical evidence of one of history's most celebrated buildings.
takeaways: The Pharos collapsed into the sea after 14th-century earthquakes
Massive stone blocks and sphinxes were found on the seafloor
The lighthouse was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World

faq.question: How tall was the Pharos of Alexandria?
faq.answer: Ancient sources estimated its height at 100-140 meters, making it one of the tallest structures in the ancient world. A fire or mirror at its summit was reportedly visible from 50 kilometers away. The three-tiered tower stood for nearly 1,600 years before earthquakes toppled it.

faq.question: What has been found of the Pharos underwater?
faq.answer: Massive granite blocks weighing up to 75 tons, sphinx statues, column drums, and architectural fragments scattered across the seafloor near the medieval Qaitbay Fort (which was built partly from Pharos rubble). The underwater debris field matches the expected size and location.
